source.title: Understanding Sharpness Dynamics in NN Training with a Minimalist Example: The Effects of Dataset Difficulty, Depth, Stochasticity, and More
source.authors: Geonhui Yoo; Minhak Song; Chulhee Yun

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no material truncation is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper experimentally measures sharpness and training-loss dynamics at the edge of stability in a minimalist model and a Transformer. This bears on part of V5, but it does not test the full-batch sharpness claim across longer training or whether rates above the initial linearized stability limit recover.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure training classification error, memorization, shortcuts, or the initialization and normalization effects in V1–V4 and V6. Its results on progressive sharpening and edge-of-stability dynamics are its own; cited results from other papers are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests V5's full-batch edge-of-stability component by tracking Hessian sharpness and training loss in a minimalist linear network and a Transformer. Its precision experiments also test conditions under which this behavior persists.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that their minimalist model reproduces progressive sharpening and edge-of-stability behavior, derive sharpness bounds tied to problem parameters, and explain batch-size and learning-rate effects through layer imbalance. They also report that numerical precision can alter self-stabilization and cause loss blowup in minimalist models.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates sharpness dynamics rather than the specific interventions and training-error outcomes in the cited original sources. Its own experiments use a single-neuron deep linear network and a two-layer Transformer.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sharpness trends varying with dataset size, depth, batch size, and learning rate in its experiments; it also reports that numerical precision changes edge-of-stability dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: Dataset difficulty, depth, batch size, and learning rate predict the degree of progressive sharpening; initialization variance affects initial sharpness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness evolution depends on data geometry, architecture, optimizer stochasticity, and initialization. Sharpness alone does not establish training-error degradation, initialization-dependent training speed, or recovery above the initial stability limit.

record.problems: The edge-of-stability comparisons are shown in figures without exact values in the text. The Transformer comparison is one architecture and dataset setting; these experiments do not test the learning-rate-above-initial-stability recovery claim in V5.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result rows were identified. Figure 1 and the other experiments report progressive-sharpening trends, but do not measure the training-error outcomes in V1–V4 or V6, nor the specific above-initial-stability recovery in V5.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, corrupted labels, and effects of capacity or training recipe.
Spurious minima in ReLU teacher-student networks and the benefit of extra student neurons.
Depth-related training-error degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization effects on learning speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth. Initialization-dependent sharpness bounds do not measure these outcomes.

Recovery versus divergence when learning rates start above the initial linearized stability limit; the wide-network catapult regime; systematic divergence despite initially subthreshold rates. The reported edge-of-stability trajectories cover finite runs, not arbitrary training horizons.
Batch normalization versus matched unnormalized networks, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training speed or stability.

missing.what: Precision-dependent sharpness and loss trajectories in the synthetic depth-2 model: JAX float32/float64 comparison and C++ precision sweep, including explicitly reported high-precision loss blowup.
Precision-dependent failure and delayed sharpness drop in the depth-2 minimalist model trained on 300 two-label CIFAR-10 samples.
Precision-dependent catapult timing without blowup in the three-layer SiLU network; trajectories overlap at precision ≥256.
missing.locator: Appendix D.2; Figure 30; width 32, N = 300, GD η = 2/200

record.verdict_notes: The record's limits_scope verdict incorrectly treats untested parts of V5 as contrary evidence. Figure 6 supports the tested component; Appendix D supplies actual scope qualifications. Figure 1 provides additional relevant sharpness/loss trajectories but is already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; model size and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of student width relative to teacher width on spurious minima.
Training error across plain and residual networks at different depths; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Whether activation-matched or orthogonal initialization improves learning speed or trainable depth.

Whether learning rates above the initial linearized stability limit cause recovery versus divergence; sharpness tracking the stability threshold over longer full-batch training; the study does not report exact numerical values for its figure-only curves.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.
